description: Wire vectors of the ApiVersions API (key 18, v0 to v5), replayed by tests/Compliance.

vectors.description: ApiVersions request v0, which has no body at all: only the common request header.
ApiVersions response v0 of the Kafka 2.8.2 container: the 56 api keys it serves on the PLAINTEXT listener, without a throttle time.
ApiVersions request v1 (Kafka 0.11): the same empty body as v0, only the api version of the header differs.
ApiVersions response v1 of the same broker: the same 56 keys followed by the throttle_time_ms that Kafka 0.11 appended.
ApiVersions request v2, the version this client sends: the KIP-219 bump of Kafka 2.0, again the header and nothing else.
ApiVersions response v2: the frame of version 1 byte for byte, because KIP-219 raised the version without changing the schema.
ApiVersions request v3, the version this client sends: the first flexible frame of the protocol - a request header v2 with a tag buffer, two compact strings of KIP-511 and a tag buffer of its own.

ApiVersions response v3 of the container: a response header v0 (the exception of KIP-511), a compact api array whose 56 entries each end in a tag buffer, and a body tag buffer that carries the finalized-features epoch 0 of KIP-584.

The answer to a v3 request whose client_software_name is "php/kafka": the error code 42 (InvalidRequest) and an empty api array, in the v3 layout - the broker matches both KIP-511 strings against [a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9\-.]*[a-zA-Z0-9])? and refuses the request before it reads anything else.
Answer to an ApiVersions request of version 4: the error code 35 and, since KIP-511, the single row of the ApiVersions api itself, in the version 0 layout.

ApiVersions request **v4**, the version this client sends since Kafka 3.9: the flexible v3 frame of KIP-511 with a **4** in its header and not one field more. "Version 4 fixes KAFKA-17011, which blocked SupportedFeatures.MinVersion in the response from being 0" is the whole comment of the bump in `ApiVersionsRequest.json` @ 3.9.2, so this frame and `apiversions.request.v3.kraft-node` differ in exactly one byte.

What the 3.9.2 KRaft node answers that request on its PLAINTEXT listener: the **61 keys** of its `broker` listener as a compact array, the trailing throttle time of KIP-124 and the three tagged fields of KIP-584. The reason the version exists is in the tagged field 0 - the node supports **two** features, `kraft.version` 0 to 1 and `metadata.version` 1 to 21, and the first of them is reported only from the version 4 on, because its minimum is 0 (`ApiVersionsResponse.maybeFilterSupportedFeatureKeys` @ 3.9.2). The finalized features name `metadata.version` at the level 21 (`3.9-IV0`) alone: a feature finalized at the level 0 is not finalized at all. The epoch is the offset of the metadata log the feature records stand at and moves with every write of the cluster.
The same request one api version lower, sent to the same node on the same listener seconds later: the api version of the header is the only byte that differs from `apiversions.request.v4`.

And the answer to it, **19 bytes shorter**: the same 61 rows, the same throttle time, the same finalized features and the same epoch, with the `kraft.version` entry missing from the supported features. Those 19 bytes are the whole of KAFKA-17011 - a client of Kafka 3.0 to 3.8 reads a `min_version` of 0 as "the feature is not there", so a broker hides such a feature from every answer below the version 4 rather than lie about its range.

ApiVersions request **v5**, the version this client sends since Kafka 4.4 (KIP-1242): the v4 frame with the `cluster_id` of the 4.4.0 node (a compact nullable string, 22 + 1) and its `node_id` 1 behind the two KIP-511 strings - the cluster and the node the connection is meant to reach.

What the 4.4.0 node answers that request: the ids name it, so the answer is the full one - the **77 keys** of its client listener, the trailing throttle time and the three tagged fields of KIP-584 with seven supported features, every one finalized at its highest level. The frame is the v4 layout: KIP-1242 added no field to the answer.
The same request of a client that knows neither id: the null cluster id (`00`) and the node id -1. The node does not check it and answers the full table, like a v4.
A v5 request that names the node id 1 of a cluster `AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA` the node does not belong to - the metadata of another cluster, as a stale cache or a reused address would give it.

The answer: the error code **129** `REBOOTSTRAP_REQUIRED`, an empty api array, the throttle time and an empty tag section - `ApiVersionsRequest.getErrorResponse()` in the layout of the version asked for, not the v0 layout of a 35. The connection stays open.
The right cluster id with the node id 2: the cluster is right, the broker at the address is not the node the client means.
The same 129 for it: `KafkaApis.handleApiVersionsRequest` @ 4.4.0 refuses a cluster id that is not its own and a node id that is not its `broker.id` alike.

Half a pair: the right cluster id next to the node id -1, which `ApiVersionsRequest.isValid()` @ 4.4.0 refuses before any id is compared ("Either cluster ID and node ID are both specified, or neither is").
The answer: the error code **42** `InvalidRequest` of the KIP-511 pattern check, empty, in the v5 layout. A node id next to the null cluster id is answered the same 42.
